svg.title: Figure 12 — The ten render passes, in draw order
svg.desc: A stack of ten slabs. The bottom slab is painted first and the top slab last. Passes one and two are screen space; the world transform is then pushed and passes three to seven are world space; the transform is popped and passes eight to ten are screen space again. Each slab names its pass, its space, and the condition under which it is skipped.
svg.text: FIGURE 12
Render passes — one function, ten passes, two coordinate spaces
renderScene() draws the screen canvas, the minimap and every export with the same code. Geometry lives in world space; every piece of text lives in screen space at a fixed point size.
PAINTED FIRST
PAINTED LAST
Background
o.background, falling back to the --canvas token
SCREEN
c.fillRect(0, 0, o.w, o.h)
Export passes an explicit background so the picture is opaque; the minimap clears first instead.
Dot grid
skipped when o.grid === false, or when the step falls below 11px
SCREEN
const step = 34 * k; if (step > 11) { … }
Drawn in screen space and offset by view.x % step, so the dots stay crisp 1.5px squares at
every zoom and the field appears to slide under the graph rather than scale with it.
c.save(); c.translate(view.x, view.y); c.scale(k, k);
— world space begins. From here every stroke width is divided by k to hold its screen weight.
Radial rings
radial layout only, centred on G.ringOrigin
WORLD
c.lineWidth = 1 / k · stroke = --canvas-grid
One arc per entry in G.radialRings. The origin is the focus node's position after centring,
not the world origin, so the rings track the tree they belong to.
Cluster frames
grid layout only, one rounded rect per block
WORLD
roundRect(c, b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h, 10) · stroke = --stroke
Frames are geometry, so they zoom. Their titles are text, so they do not — see pass 8.
Edges
three routings: orthogonal in hierarchy, fanned when parallel, otherwise straight
WORLD
alpha: hovered 1 · non-adjacent 0.18 · structural 0.72 · incidental 0.48
rdf:type is dashed at [5/k, 5/k]. Parallel edges between the same pair are offset by
(mi − (mn − 1) / 2) × 22 along the normal, so they fan instead of stacking.
Arrowheads
skipped entirely below 42% zoom
WORLD
if (k > 0.42) { … } tip at b.r + 2.5 back along the edge · size 6 / k
The tip is set back by the target's radius so the head touches the shape, not its centre.
Direction is taken from the last control point, so a fanned edge points along its curve.
Nodes
selection ring, shape fill, defined mark, focus outline, pin dot — in that order
WORLD
ring r + 7/k at 2.5/k · focus outline r + 3/k at 1.8/k · pin dot 3.4/k + 1
Hovering dims every node that is not the hovered node or one of its neighbours to alpha 0.25.
See Figure 19 for the full encoding of shape, colour and marker.
c.restore();
— world space ends. Text from here on is placed by projecting world coordinates by hand.
Cluster titles
grid layout only, and only above 22% zoom
SCREEN
sx = b.x * k + view.x + 12 · sy = b.y * k + view.y + 22
600 12px for the label, 400 11px for the count, offset 46 past the measured label width.
Culled when the projected origin falls more than 200px outside the viewport.
Node labels
greedy collision pass — see Figure 13
SCREEN
strokeText with the background colour at 3.5px, then fillText — a halo, not a box
600 12.5px for entities, 400 11px for individuals. Capped at 900 labels on screen and
4,000 in an export, because an export is read at a size a screen never is.
Hidden-neighbour badges
skipped when o.badges === false, or below 30% zoom
SCREEN
A 14px pill on the node's upper right, filled with --surface and stroked, so it stays
readable over any node colour. Last pass, so nothing can paint over it.
What is not in renderScene()
drawMinimap() paints a second canvas from the same node set, with no labels, no badges
and no grid — a shape, not a reading surface.
drawExportChrome() runs after renderScene() on the export canvas only, adding the header
band and the legend footer. See Figure 18.
Neither is ever drawn on the workbench canvas, and renderScene() knows about neither.
The rule the split enforces
Anything that carries meaning through its position and
size is world space, and zooms.
Anything that has to be read — a label, a count, a
badge, a title — is screen space, and does not.
Type never shrinks below its designed size.
Figure 12 · Render passes. Illustrates 22-graph-rendering-and-export.md, “Draw order” and “World space and screen space”. [src: renderScene(), draw(), drawMinimap()]
